_**Ted**_ (stylized in all lowercase) is a 2012 American fantasystoner comedy film directed and co-produced by Seth MacFarlane and written by MacFarlane, Alec Sulkin, and Wellesley Wild based on a story written by MacFarlane. The first installment in the _Ted_ franchise, the film stars Mark Wahlberg and Mila Kunis, with Joel McHale and Giovanni Ribisi in supporting roles, and MacFarlane providing the voice and motion capture of the title character. The story follows John Bennett, a Boston native whose childhood wish brings his teddy bear friend Ted to life. However, in adulthood, their friendship begins to interfere with the progression of John's work life and his relationship with his girlfriend, Lori Collins.
The feature directorial debut of MacFarlane, the film premiered at the [Grauman's Chinese Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grauman's_Chinese_Theatre "Grauman's Chinese Theatre") on June 21, 2012, and was theatrically released in the United States on June 29 by Universal Pictures. It received positive reviews from critics and was a commercial success, grossing $549 million worldwide. _Ted_ was the highest-grossing comedy film of the year and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Original Song. The film also successfully launched a franchise, with a sequel released in 2015, a prequel television series released from 2024 to 2026, and a 2026 animated sequel series.

In 1985, 8-year-old John Bennett is a friendless only child living in Norwood, Massachusetts. On Christmas Day, he wishes for his new gift, a jumbo teddy bear named Ted, to come to life and become his friend. The wish coincides with a shooting star and comes true; word spreads, and Ted briefly becomes a celebrity.
In 2012, the now 35-year-old John and Ted are still living together in an apartment in Boston with John's girlfriend Lori Collins, and are staunch companions enjoying a hedonistic life. As the couple's fourth anniversary approaches, Lori hopes to marry John, but feels he cannot move forward in life with Ted around. He is hesitant about making Ted leave, but is persuaded to act when they find Ted at home with a group of prostitutes, including one who defecated on the floor, while they were out for their anniversary dinner.
John finds Ted his own apartment and a job at a grocery store, where he begins dating his co-worker, Tami-Lynn. Lori learns that John has been skipping work, using her as an excuse, to spend most of his time with Ted. John and Lori are invited to a party put on by Lori's womanizing manager Rex, but Ted lures John away to a party at his apartment with the offer to meet Sam J. Jones, the star of their favorite film, _Flash Gordon_.
Intending to stay only for a few minutes, John gets caught up in the occasion. Lori finds John there and kicks him out of their apartment, breaking up with him. Devastated and furious, he blames Ted for ruining his life and ends their friendship.
Ted then goes to John's hotel room to inform him that Lori and Rex are attending a Norah Jones concert on a date together. Their conversation becomes an argument and then a violent brawl, but they reconcile. To repair John's relationship with Lori, Ted arranges for Norah Jones, an old lover of his, to help by having John express his love for Lori with a song during Norah's concert.

John does an off-key rendition of "All Time High", the theme song of _Octopussy_, which he and Lori watched on their first date. He is booed off stage, though the attempt touches Lori. She returns to her apartment, where Ted confesses to his role in John's relapse and offers to leave them alone forever if she talks to John, to which Lori agrees.
After Lori leaves, however, Ted is kidnapped by Donny, an obsessive stalker who has idolized him since he was a child. Donny plans to make Ted into his son Robert's new toy. Ted obtains a phone to contact John, but is recaptured.
Realizing Ted is in danger, John and Lori locate Donny's residence and track him. They chase them to Fenway Park, where Donny rips Ted in half. Two police cars arrive, forcing Donny to flee the scene. John and Lori gather Ted's stuffing, and Ted relays his wish for John to be happy with Lori before the magic in Ted fades away, making him a normal teddy bear again.
Unable to accept his death, John and Lori unsuccessfully attempt to repair Ted. Saddened by the incident, Lori makes a wish upon a shooting star. The following day, Ted is magically restored due to the wish and reunites with John and Lori. John finally proposes to her, and she accepts. Sometime later, John and Lori get married (with Sam Jones as the presiding minister).
In the film's epilogue, the narrator says that Ted comfortably accepted having a life of his own, as he and Tami-Lynn continued their love affair; Sam Jones attempts to restart his film career and moves into a studio apartment with Brandon Routh; Rex gives up his pursuit of Lori, goes into a deep depression, and dies of Lou Gehrig's disease; Donny gets arrested by the Boston Police Department for kidnapping Ted, but the charges are dropped, due to the situation sounding ridiculous. Robert hires a personal trainer, loses a significant amount of weight, and goes on to become Taylor Lautner.

Seth MacFarlane co-wrote, co-produced, and directed the film, and provided the motion capture and the voice for the title character.

This film serves as the feature directorial debut of Seth MacFarlane, his first time as director in any capacity. Compared to most of his other work, such as _Family Guy_, _American Dad!_, and _The Cleveland Show_, this film is a live-action effort, with computer animation handled by visual effects facilities Tippett Studio and Iloura. MacFarlane wrote the screenplay with his _Family Guy_ colleagues Alec Sulkin and Wellesley Wild based on a story idea written by MacFarlane himself.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-MK-7) MacFarlane originally wanted to make _Ted_ into an animated television show, much like his previous works, and later revealed in an interview with TheWrap ahead of the release of the prequel series in 2024 that he had pitched the idea as a family-oriented series during his time working at Hanna-Barbera, wherein Ted would be what MacFarlane described as a "leech on the family" as the boy went on to grow up, go to college and start said family. While MacFarlane himself admitted he "never did anything with" the original incarnation of the project, he came back to it when considering ideas for his first feature film, realizing it "seemed like an idea that had some legs... and since it was a movie instead of a TV show and an ongoing group of characters, it seemed like telling a love story from start to finish and using that framework was maybe a better way to go. So the dad became a single guy trying to get his relationship back together".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-9)

Originally, 20th Century Fox was offered to finance and distribute the film, given their production partnership with _Family Guy_, _American Dad!_, and _The Cleveland Show_, all created by MacFarlane. However, MacFarlane wanted a budget of $65 million for the film, which Fox considered to be too high for an R-rated comedy film, let alone one from a first-time director, and was skeptical about the film's future success. They also wanted it to be rated PG-13 instead of R, which MacFarlane, Sulkin, and Wild ended up writing a version of. However, despite this, Fox backed out, and MacFarlane began to take the project elsewhere.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-10) MacFarlane later set up the project at Media Rights Capital, and on April 12, 2010, Universal Pictures announced that it had acquired the full rights to _Ted_ after it agreed to the $65 million budget he requested and to direct the R-rated version of the script.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-deadline-budget-5)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-11)

On October 26, 2010, Mark Wahlberg joined the project as the lead actor opposite MacFarlane;[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-MK-7)Matt Damon in 2026 said he had been offered the role, but declined.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-12) Two months later, on December 14, Mila Kunis, MacFarlane's _Family Guy_ co-star, also joined the cast; it is Wahlberg and Kunis' second collaboration following 2008's _Max Payne_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-13) On February 23, 2011, Giovanni Ribisi signed on to the film to play the film's villain.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-14) Filming began in May 2011 in Boston, Norwood and other locations in Massachusetts.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-15)
The film was scheduled for release in the United States on July 13, 2012, but it was moved up to June 29, both to avoid competition with _Ice Age: Continental Drift_ and following the delay of _G.I. Joe: Retaliation_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-16) Internationally, the film was released in Australia on July 5, 2012,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-17) and on August 1, 2012, in the United Kingdom and Ireland.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-18)

The film's soundtrack was released by Universal Republic Records on June 26, 2012. It features the score by Walter Murphy and songs by various artists such as Norah Jones and Queen. Seth MacFarlane co-wrote the opening theme "Everybody Needs a Best Friend" with Murphy.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-19) The song was later nominated for the Academy Award for Best Original Song at the 85th Academy Awards.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-20)
To promote the film, Universal Pictures teamed up with Axe in a marketing campaign that involved the title character and the brand's hair care product Axe Hair.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-21) In one commercial, Ted takes a woman on a date to a fancy restaurant, where he brings her to orgasm under the table before handing another man a box of Axe Hair gel.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-22)
To promote the film in Japan, United International Pictures teamed up with Spike Chunsoft in a marketing campaign that involved the title character and _Danganronpa_bearmascotMonokuma.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-23)
In February 2013, Wahlberg and MacFarlane (as Ted) made an appearance at the 85th Academy Awards, which MacFarlane himself hosted.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-24)

_Ted_ grossed $218.8 million in North America and $330.6 million overseas for a total gross of $549.4 million, against a budget of $50 million.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-BoxOfficeMojo-4) It was Universal's highest-grossing film in 2012, ahead of _Snow White and the Huntsman_ and _Battleship_[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-World_record-25) (the only one to pass $400 million[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-09/18-26)), and the 12th-highest-grossing film of 2012.
_Ted_ debuted in first place in Taiwan and got the best comedy opening ever there.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-Australia_Record-27) It also debuted in Hong Kong, with $1.4 million, and grossed $571,000 in its first week in South Korea,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-28) eventually grossing $8 million, $3.8 million and $1.8 million respectively.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-ForeignGross-29) It also grossed $2.1 million in both Indonesia and Singapore, and $1.4 million in Thailand.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-ForeignGross-29)

In January 2013, the film opened at number one in Japan, its final market, with $4.5 million, the best start ever for an R-rated comedy there. In comparison, it grossed more in its opening weekend than _The Hangover Part II_ made in its entire run.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-30) The following weekend, it retained the number one spot for the second consecutive frame, grossing $3.6 million at 137 dates, for a 10-day market cumulative total of $11.2 million.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-31) By its third weekend, the film stayed at the number one spot for a third week, with earning down less than 10%, pushing _Ted_'s overseas total past the $300 million mark, and making it the top grossing R-rated comedy of all time in Japan.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-32) It then had its fourth consecutive weekend at number one, drawing another $3 million at 354 locations in the country.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-33) Its cumulative total stands at $44 million grossed.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-34)
_Ted_ debuted with $14.3 million in the United Kingdom, making it the third-best debut ever for a Universal film behind _Bridget Jones: The Edge of Reason_ and _King Kong_,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-Foreign1-35) eventually grossing over $48.9 million in the country. _Ted_ was released in cinemas across the United Kingdom on August 3.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-ForeignGross-29)

_Ted_ also debuted at number one in Australia and New Zealand, grossing over $35.5 million and $3.5 million respectively.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-ForeignGross-29) Its $13.1 million opening in Australia, of which $4.5 million were from previews, was Universal's biggest opening ever in the country.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-Australia_Record-27) In Australia, _Ted_ was rated MA 15+,[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-Aus-49) whereas in New Zealand, it was rated R13 for its theatrical release and R16 for the extended DVD/Blu-ray release.
South America  
In Brazil, the film opened with $1.4 million at 273 sites,[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-50) moving up to 1st place in the country on its third week of release.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-51) It has since grossed $8.8 million there.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-ForeignGross-29)
The film also grossed $4.6 million in Argentina, 2 million in Chile, 1.9 million in Peru, and 1.7 million in Colombia.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-ForeignGross-29)

Most of the reviews _Ted_ received were positive.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-54)On the review aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes, 68% of 219 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 6.40/10.The website's consensus reads: "_Ted_'s 'romance versus bromance' plot is familiar, but the film's held aloft by the high-concept central premise and a very funny (albeit inconsistent) script."[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-Rotten_Tomatoes-55) On Metacritic, the film has an average score of 62 out of 100 based on 37 critics, indicating "generally favorable reviews".[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-Metacritic-56) Audiences polled by CinemaScore gave the film an average grade of "A−" on an A+ to F scale.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-CinemaScore-57)
Roger Ebert gave the film three-and-a-half stars out of four, citing the film as "the best comedy screenplay so far [this year]," also praising the film on the fact that it "doesn't run out of steam."[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-RE-58)Nathan Rabin of _The A.V. Club_ gave the film a "B" grade.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-AVClub-59) On the other hand, A.O. Scott of _The New York Times_ called _Ted_ "boring, lazy and wildly unoriginal."[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-NYT-60)

Director Paul Thomas Anderson has stated that he is a big fan of the film, calling it great and also putting it on his favorite films of the 21st century list.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-62)
The film was released on DVD and Blu-ray in the United States on December 11, 2012, by Universal Studios Home Entertainment.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-78) Both formats featured an unrated version of the film (112 minutes) and were also released in Australia on November 21, 2012, in an "Extended Edition".[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-79) It was released on DVD and Blu-ray in the United Kingdom on November 26, 2012.
On May 3, 2016, _Ted vs. Flash Gordon: The Ultimate Collection_ was released on Blu-ray plus Digital HD, featuring _Flash Gordon_ and the unrated versions of _Ted_ and _Ted 2_.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-80)
_Ted_ was released on 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray as a [collector's edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collector's_edition "Collector's edition") on December 10, 2024, by Shout! Factory.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-81)
In Brazil, the movie was the target of a complaint from a member of the PCDB party, who denounced the film for promoting drug use and requested its suspension, calling it absurd.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-82)

During the 2012 _American Dad!_Comic-Con panel, MacFarlane stated that he would be open to a sequel to _Ted_.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-83) In September 2012, chief executive Steve Burke said that the studio would be looking to make a sequel to _Ted_ "as soon as possible".[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-84)
On _Anderson Live_, Wahlberg confirmed that a sequel was in the works and that it would be the first sequel in his career, while also revealing that he and Ted (as voiced by MacFarlane) would appear at the 85th Academy Awards.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-85)
In February 2014, _Deadline_ reported that Amanda Seyfried had been cast as the female lead, and that Kunis would not return.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-86) On July 8, MacFarlane announced that work had officially begun on the sequel.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-87)_Ted 2_ was released in the United States on June 26, 2015.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-88) It was neither critically nor financially as successful, though it still turned a profit, grossing $215.9 million on a $68 million budget.

_**Ted**_ (stylized in all lowercase) is a 2012 American fantasystoner comedy film directed and co-produced by Seth MacFarlane and written by MacFarlane, Alec Sulkin, and Wellesley Wild based on a story written by MacFarlane. The first installment in the _Ted_ franchise, the film stars Mark Wahlberg and Mila Kunis, with Joel McHale and Giovanni Ribisi in supporting roles, and MacFarlane providing the voice and motion capture of the title character. The story follows John Bennett, a Boston native whose childhood wish brings his teddy bear friend Ted to life. However, in adulthood, their friendship begins to interfere with the progression of John's work life and his relationship with his girlfriend, Lori Collins.
The feature directorial debut of MacFarlane, the film premiered at the [Grauman's Chinese Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grauman's_Chinese_Theatre "Grauman's Chinese Theatre") on June 21, 2012, and was theatrically released in the United States on June 29 by Universal Pictures. It received positive reviews from critics and was a commercial success, grossing $549 million worldwide. _Ted_ was the highest-grossing comedy film of the year and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Original Song. The film also successfully launched a franchise, with a sequel released in 2015, a prequel television series released from 2024 to 2026, and a 2026 animated sequel series.

In 1985, 8-year-old John Bennett is a friendless only child living in Norwood, Massachusetts. On Christmas Day, he wishes for his new gift, a jumbo teddy bear named Ted, to come to life and become his friend. The wish coincides with a shooting star and comes true; word spreads, and Ted briefly becomes a celebrity.
In 2012, the now 35-year-old John and Ted are still living together in an apartment in Boston with John's girlfriend Lori Collins, and are staunch companions enjoying a hedonistic life. As the couple's fourth anniversary approaches, Lori hopes to marry John, but feels he cannot move forward in life with Ted around. He is hesitant about making Ted leave, but is persuaded to act when they find Ted at home with a group of prostitutes, including one who defecated on the floor, while they were out for their anniversary dinner.
John finds Ted his own apartment and a job at a grocery store, where he begins dating his co-worker, Tami-Lynn. Lori learns that John has been skipping work, using her as an excuse, to spend most of his time with Ted. John and Lori are invited to a party put on by Lori's womanizing manager Rex, but Ted lures John away to a party at his apartment with the offer to meet Sam J. Jones, the star of their favorite film, _Flash Gordon_.
Intending to stay only for a few minutes, John gets caught up in the occasion. Lori finds John there and kicks him out of their apartment, breaking up with him. Devastated and furious, he blames Ted for ruining his life and ends their friendship.
Ted then goes to John's hotel room to inform him that Lori and Rex are attending a Norah Jones concert on a date together. Their conversation becomes an argument and then a violent brawl, but they reconcile. To repair John's relationship with Lori, Ted arranges for Norah Jones, an old lover of his, to help by having John express his love for Lori with a song during Norah's concert.
texts.3:
John does an off-key rendition of "All Time High", the theme song of _Octopussy_, which he and Lori watched on their first date. He is booed off stage, though the attempt touches Lori. She returns to her apartment, where Ted confesses to his role in John's relapse and offers to leave them alone forever if she talks to John, to which Lori agrees.
After Lori leaves, however, Ted is kidnapped by Donny, an obsessive stalker who has idolized him since he was a child. Donny plans to make Ted into his son Robert's new toy. Ted obtains a phone to contact John, but is recaptured.
Realizing Ted is in danger, John and Lori locate Donny's residence and track him. They chase them to Fenway Park, where Donny rips Ted in half. Two police cars arrive, forcing Donny to flee the scene. John and Lori gather Ted's stuffing, and Ted relays his wish for John to be happy with Lori before the magic in Ted fades away, making him a normal teddy bear again.
Unable to accept his death, John and Lori unsuccessfully attempt to repair Ted. Saddened by the incident, Lori makes a wish upon a shooting star. The following day, Ted is magically restored due to the wish and reunites with John and Lori. John finally proposes to her, and she accepts. Sometime later, John and Lori get married (with Sam Jones as the presiding minister).
In the film's epilogue, the narrator says that Ted comfortably accepted having a life of his own, as he and Tami-Lynn continued their love affair; Sam Jones attempts to restart his film career and moves into a studio apartment with Brandon Routh; Rex gives up his pursuit of Lori, goes into a deep depression, and dies of Lou Gehrig's disease; Donny gets arrested by the Boston Police Department for kidnapping Ted, but the charges are dropped, due to the situation sounding ridiculous. Robert hires a personal trainer, loses a significant amount of weight, and goes on to become Taylor Lautner.

texts.6: This film serves as the feature directorial debut of Seth MacFarlane, his first time as director in any capacity. Compared to most of his other work, such as _Family Guy_, _American Dad!_, and _The Cleveland Show_, this film is a live-action effort, with computer animation handled by visual effects facilities Tippett Studio and Iloura. MacFarlane wrote the screenplay with his _Family Guy_ colleagues Alec Sulkin and Wellesley Wild based on a story idea written by MacFarlane himself.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-MK-7) MacFarlane originally wanted to make _Ted_ into an animated television show, much like his previous works, and later revealed in an interview with TheWrap ahead of the release of the prequel series in 2024 that he had pitched the idea as a family-oriented series during his time working at Hanna-Barbera, wherein Ted would be what MacFarlane described as a "leech on the family" as the boy went on to grow up, go to college and start said family. While MacFarlane himself admitted he "never did anything with" the original incarnation of the project, he came back to it when considering ideas for his first feature film, realizing it "seemed like an idea that had some legs... and since it was a movie instead of a TV show and an ongoing group of characters, it seemed like telling a love story from start to finish and using that framework was maybe a better way to go. So the dad became a single guy trying to get his relationship back together".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-9)
texts.7: Originally, 20th Century Fox was offered to finance and distribute the film, given their production partnership with _Family Guy_, _American Dad!_, and _The Cleveland Show_, all created by MacFarlane. However, MacFarlane wanted a budget of $65 million for the film, which Fox considered to be too high for an R-rated comedy film, let alone one from a first-time director, and was skeptical about the film's future success. They also wanted it to be rated PG-13 instead of R, which MacFarlane, Sulkin, and Wild ended up writing a version of. However, despite this, Fox backed out, and MacFarlane began to take the project elsewhere.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-10) MacFarlane later set up the project at Media Rights Capital, and on April 12, 2010, Universal Pictures announced that it had acquired the full rights to _Ted_ after it agreed to the $65 million budget he requested and to direct the R-rated version of the script.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-deadline-budget-5)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-11)

The film's soundtrack was released by Universal Republic Records on June 26, 2012. It features the score by Walter Murphy and songs by various artists such as Norah Jones and Queen. Seth MacFarlane co-wrote the opening theme "Everybody Needs a Best Friend" with Murphy.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-19) The song was later nominated for the Academy Award for Best Original Song at the 85th Academy Awards.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-20)
To promote the film, Universal Pictures teamed up with Axe in a marketing campaign that involved the title character and the brand's hair care product Axe Hair.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-21) In one commercial, Ted takes a woman on a date to a fancy restaurant, where he brings her to orgasm under the table before handing another man a box of Axe Hair gel.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-22)
To promote the film in Japan, United International Pictures teamed up with Spike Chunsoft in a marketing campaign that involved the title character and _Danganronpa_bearmascotMonokuma.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-23)
In February 2013, Wahlberg and MacFarlane (as Ted) made an appearance at the 85th Academy Awards, which MacFarlane himself hosted.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-24)
texts.10:
_Ted_ grossed $218.8 million in North America and $330.6 million overseas for a total gross of $549.4 million, against a budget of $50 million.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-BoxOfficeMojo-4) It was Universal's highest-grossing film in 2012, ahead of _Snow White and the Huntsman_ and _Battleship_[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-World_record-25) (the only one to pass $400 million[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-09/18-26)), and the 12th-highest-grossing film of 2012.
_Ted_ debuted in first place in Taiwan and got the best comedy opening ever there.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-Australia_Record-27) It also debuted in Hong Kong, with $1.4 million, and grossed $571,000 in its first week in South Korea,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-28) eventually grossing $8 million, $3.8 million and $1.8 million respectively.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-ForeignGross-29) It also grossed $2.1 million in both Indonesia and Singapore, and $1.4 million in Thailand.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-ForeignGross-29)
texts.11:
In January 2013, the film opened at number one in Japan, its final market, with $4.5 million, the best start ever for an R-rated comedy there. In comparison, it grossed more in its opening weekend than _The Hangover Part II_ made in its entire run.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-30) The following weekend, it retained the number one spot for the second consecutive frame, grossing $3.6 million at 137 dates, for a 10-day market cumulative total of $11.2 million.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-31) By its third weekend, the film stayed at the number one spot for a third week, with earning down less than 10%, pushing _Ted_'s overseas total past the $300 million mark, and making it the top grossing R-rated comedy of all time in Japan.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-32) It then had its fourth consecutive weekend at number one, drawing another $3 million at 354 locations in the country.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-33) Its cumulative total stands at $44 million grossed.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-34)
_Ted_ debuted with $14.3 million in the United Kingdom, making it the third-best debut ever for a Universal film behind _Bridget Jones: The Edge of Reason_ and _King Kong_,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-Foreign1-35) eventually grossing over $48.9 million in the country. _Ted_ was released in cinemas across the United Kingdom on August 3.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-ForeignGross-29)
texts.15:
_Ted_ also debuted at number one in Australia and New Zealand, grossing over $35.5 million and $3.5 million respectively.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-ForeignGross-29) Its $13.1 million opening in Australia, of which $4.5 million were from previews, was Universal's biggest opening ever in the country.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-Australia_Record-27) In Australia, _Ted_ was rated MA 15+,[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-Aus-49) whereas in New Zealand, it was rated R13 for its theatrical release and R16 for the extended DVD/Blu-ray release.
South America

The film also grossed $4.6 million in Argentina, 2 million in Chile, 1.9 million in Peru, and 1.7 million in Colombia.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-ForeignGross-29)

Most of the reviews _Ted_ received were positive.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-54)On the review aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes, 68% of 219 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 6.40/10.The website's consensus reads: "_Ted_'s 'romance versus bromance' plot is familiar, but the film's held aloft by the high-concept central premise and a very funny (albeit inconsistent) script."[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-Rotten_Tomatoes-55) On Metacritic, the film has an average score of 62 out of 100 based on 37 critics, indicating "generally favorable reviews".[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-Metacritic-56) Audiences polled by CinemaScore gave the film an average grade of "A−" on an A+ to F scale.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-CinemaScore-57)
Roger Ebert gave the film three-and-a-half stars out of four, citing the film as "the best comedy screenplay so far [this year]," also praising the film on the fact that it "doesn't run out of steam."[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-RE-58)Nathan Rabin of _The A.V. Club_ gave the film a "B" grade.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-AVClub-59) On the other hand, A.O. Scott of _The New York Times_ called _Ted_ "boring, lazy and wildly unoriginal."[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-NYT-60)

Director Paul Thomas Anderson has stated that he is a big fan of the film, calling it great and also putting it on his favorite films of the 21st century list.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-62)
The film was released on DVD and Blu-ray in the United States on December 11, 2012, by Universal Studios Home Entertainment.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-78) Both formats featured an unrated version of the film (112 minutes) and were also released in Australia on November 21, 2012, in an "Extended Edition".[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-79) It was released on DVD and Blu-ray in the United Kingdom on November 26, 2012.
On May 3, 2016, _Ted vs. Flash Gordon: The Ultimate Collection_ was released on Blu-ray plus Digital HD, featuring _Flash Gordon_ and the unrated versions of _Ted_ and _Ted 2_.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-80)
_Ted_ was released on 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray as a [collector's edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collector's_edition "Collector's edition") on December 10, 2024, by Shout! Factory.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-81)
In Brazil, the movie was the target of a complaint from a member of the PCDB party, who denounced the film for promoting drug use and requested its suspension, calling it absurd.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-82)

During the 2012 _American Dad!_Comic-Con panel, MacFarlane stated that he would be open to a sequel to _Ted_.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-83) In September 2012, chief executive Steve Burke said that the studio would be looking to make a sequel to _Ted_ "as soon as possible".[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-84)
On _Anderson Live_, Wahlberg confirmed that a sequel was in the works and that it would be the first sequel in his career, while also revealing that he and Ted (as voiced by MacFarlane) would appear at the 85th Academy Awards.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-85)
In February 2014, _Deadline_ reported that Amanda Seyfried had been cast as the female lead, and that Kunis would not return.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-86) On July 8, MacFarlane announced that work had officially begun on the sequel.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-87)_Ted 2_ was released in the United States on June 26, 2015.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-88) It was neither critically nor financially as successful, though it still turned a profit, grossing $215.9 million on a $68 million budget.

_**Ted**_ (stylized in all lowercase) is a 2012 American fantasystoner comedy film directed and co-produced by Seth MacFarlane and written by MacFarlane, Alec Sulkin, and Wellesley Wild based on a story written by MacFarlane. The first installment in the _Ted_ franchise, the film stars Mark Wahlberg and Mila Kunis, with Joel McHale and Giovanni Ribisi in supporting roles, and MacFarlane providing the voice and motion capture of the title character. The story follows John Bennett, a Boston native whose childhood wish brings his teddy bear friend Ted to life. However, in adulthood, their friendship begins to interfere with the progression of John's work life and his relationship with his girlfriend, Lori Collins.
The feature directorial debut of MacFarlane, the film premiered at the [Grauman's Chinese Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grauman's_Chinese_Theatre "Grauman's Chinese Theatre") on June 21, 2012, and was theatrically released in the United States on June 29 by Universal Pictures. It received positive reviews from critics and was a commercial success, grossing $549 million worldwide. _Ted_ was the highest-grossing comedy film of the year and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Original Song. The film also successfully launched a franchise, with a sequel released in 2015, a prequel television series released from 2024 to 2026, and a 2026 animated sequel series.

In 1985, 8-year-old John Bennett is a friendless only child living in Norwood, Massachusetts. On Christmas Day, he wishes for his new gift, a jumbo teddy bear named Ted, to come to life and become his friend. The wish coincides with a shooting star and comes true; word spreads, and Ted briefly becomes a celebrity.
In 2012, the now 35-year-old John and Ted are still living together in an apartment in Boston with John's girlfriend Lori Collins, and are staunch companions enjoying a hedonistic life. As the couple's fourth anniversary approaches, Lori hopes to marry John, but feels he cannot move forward in life with Ted around. He is hesitant about making Ted leave, but is persuaded to act when they find Ted at home with a group of prostitutes, including one who defecated on the floor, while they were out for their anniversary dinner.
John finds Ted his own apartment and a job at a grocery store, where he begins dating his co-worker, Tami-Lynn. Lori learns that John has been skipping work, using her as an excuse, to spend most of his time with Ted. John and Lori are invited to a party put on by Lori's womanizing manager Rex, but Ted lures John away to a party at his apartment with the offer to meet Sam J. Jones, the star of their favorite film, _Flash Gordon_.
Intending to stay only for a few minutes, John gets caught up in the occasion. Lori finds John there and kicks him out of their apartment, breaking up with him. Devastated and furious, he blames Ted for ruining his life and ends their friendship.
Ted then goes to John's hotel room to inform him that Lori and Rex are attending a Norah Jones concert on a date together. Their conversation becomes an argument and then a violent brawl, but they reconcile. To repair John's relationship with Lori, Ted arranges for Norah Jones, an old lover of his, to help by having John express his love for Lori with a song during Norah's concert.

John does an off-key rendition of "All Time High", the theme song of _Octopussy_, which he and Lori watched on their first date. He is booed off stage, though the attempt touches Lori. She returns to her apartment, where Ted confesses to his role in John's relapse and offers to leave them alone forever if she talks to John, to which Lori agrees.
After Lori leaves, however, Ted is kidnapped by Donny, an obsessive stalker who has idolized him since he was a child. Donny plans to make Ted into his son Robert's new toy. Ted obtains a phone to contact John, but is recaptured.
Realizing Ted is in danger, John and Lori locate Donny's residence and track him. They chase them to Fenway Park, where Donny rips Ted in half. Two police cars arrive, forcing Donny to flee the scene. John and Lori gather Ted's stuffing, and Ted relays his wish for John to be happy with Lori before the magic in Ted fades away, making him a normal teddy bear again.
Unable to accept his death, John and Lori unsuccessfully attempt to repair Ted. Saddened by the incident, Lori makes a wish upon a shooting star. The following day, Ted is magically restored due to the wish and reunites with John and Lori. John finally proposes to her, and she accepts. Sometime later, John and Lori get married (with Sam Jones as the presiding minister).
In the film's epilogue, the narrator says that Ted comfortably accepted having a life of his own, as he and Tami-Lynn continued their love affair; Sam Jones attempts to restart his film career and moves into a studio apartment with Brandon Routh; Rex gives up his pursuit of Lori, goes into a deep depression, and dies of Lou Gehrig's disease; Donny gets arrested by the Boston Police Department for kidnapping Ted, but the charges are dropped, due to the situation sounding ridiculous. Robert hires a personal trainer, loses a significant amount of weight, and goes on to become Taylor Lautner.

Seth MacFarlane co-wrote, co-produced, and directed the film, and provided the motion capture and the voice for the title character.

This film serves as the feature directorial debut of Seth MacFarlane, his first time as director in any capacity. Compared to most of his other work, such as _Family Guy_, _American Dad!_, and _The Cleveland Show_, this film is a live-action effort, with computer animation handled by visual effects facilities Tippett Studio and Iloura. MacFarlane wrote the screenplay with his _Family Guy_ colleagues Alec Sulkin and Wellesley Wild based on a story idea written by MacFarlane himself.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-MK-7) MacFarlane originally wanted to make _Ted_ into an animated television show, much like his previous works, and later revealed in an interview with TheWrap ahead of the release of the prequel series in 2024 that he had pitched the idea as a family-oriented series during his time working at Hanna-Barbera, wherein Ted would be what MacFarlane described as a "leech on the family" as the boy went on to grow up, go to college and start said family. While MacFarlane himself admitted he "never did anything with" the original incarnation of the project, he came back to it when considering ideas for his first feature film, realizing it "seemed like an idea that had some legs... and since it was a movie instead of a TV show and an ongoing group of characters, it seemed like telling a love story from start to finish and using that framework was maybe a better way to go. So the dad became a single guy trying to get his relationship back together".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-9)

Originally, 20th Century Fox was offered to finance and distribute the film, given their production partnership with _Family Guy_, _American Dad!_, and _The Cleveland Show_, all created by MacFarlane. However, MacFarlane wanted a budget of $65 million for the film, which Fox considered to be too high for an R-rated comedy film, let alone one from a first-time director, and was skeptical about the film's future success. They also wanted it to be rated PG-13 instead of R, which MacFarlane, Sulkin, and Wild ended up writing a version of. However, despite this, Fox backed out, and MacFarlane began to take the project elsewhere.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-10) MacFarlane later set up the project at Media Rights Capital, and on April 12, 2010, Universal Pictures announced that it had acquired the full rights to _Ted_ after it agreed to the $65 million budget he requested and to direct the R-rated version of the script.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-deadline-budget-5)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-11)

On October 26, 2010, Mark Wahlberg joined the project as the lead actor opposite MacFarlane;[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-MK-7)Matt Damon in 2026 said he had been offered the role, but declined.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-12) Two months later, on December 14, Mila Kunis, MacFarlane's _Family Guy_ co-star, also joined the cast; it is Wahlberg and Kunis' second collaboration following 2008's _Max Payne_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-13) On February 23, 2011, Giovanni Ribisi signed on to the film to play the film's villain.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-14) Filming began in May 2011 in Boston, Norwood and other locations in Massachusetts.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-15)
The film was scheduled for release in the United States on July 13, 2012, but it was moved up to June 29, both to avoid competition with _Ice Age: Continental Drift_ and following the delay of _G.I. Joe: Retaliation_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-16) Internationally, the film was released in Australia on July 5, 2012,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-17) and on August 1, 2012, in the United Kingdom and Ireland.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-18)

The film's soundtrack was released by Universal Republic Records on June 26, 2012. It features the score by Walter Murphy and songs by various artists such as Norah Jones and Queen. Seth MacFarlane co-wrote the opening theme "Everybody Needs a Best Friend" with Murphy.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-19) The song was later nominated for the Academy Award for Best Original Song at the 85th Academy Awards.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-20)
To promote the film, Universal Pictures teamed up with Axe in a marketing campaign that involved the title character and the brand's hair care product Axe Hair.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-21) In one commercial, Ted takes a woman on a date to a fancy restaurant, where he brings her to orgasm under the table before handing another man a box of Axe Hair gel.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-22)
To promote the film in Japan, United International Pictures teamed up with Spike Chunsoft in a marketing campaign that involved the title character and _Danganronpa_bearmascotMonokuma.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-23)
In February 2013, Wahlberg and MacFarlane (as Ted) made an appearance at the 85th Academy Awards, which MacFarlane himself hosted.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-24)

_Ted_ grossed $218.8 million in North America and $330.6 million overseas for a total gross of $549.4 million, against a budget of $50 million.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-BoxOfficeMojo-4) It was Universal's highest-grossing film in 2012, ahead of _Snow White and the Huntsman_ and _Battleship_[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-World_record-25) (the only one to pass $400 million[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-09/18-26)), and the 12th-highest-grossing film of 2012.
_Ted_ debuted in first place in Taiwan and got the best comedy opening ever there.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-Australia_Record-27) It also debuted in Hong Kong, with $1.4 million, and grossed $571,000 in its first week in South Korea,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-28) eventually grossing $8 million, $3.8 million and $1.8 million respectively.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-ForeignGross-29) It also grossed $2.1 million in both Indonesia and Singapore, and $1.4 million in Thailand.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-ForeignGross-29)

In January 2013, the film opened at number one in Japan, its final market, with $4.5 million, the best start ever for an R-rated comedy there. In comparison, it grossed more in its opening weekend than _The Hangover Part II_ made in its entire run.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-30) The following weekend, it retained the number one spot for the second consecutive frame, grossing $3.6 million at 137 dates, for a 10-day market cumulative total of $11.2 million.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-31) By its third weekend, the film stayed at the number one spot for a third week, with earning down less than 10%, pushing _Ted_'s overseas total past the $300 million mark, and making it the top grossing R-rated comedy of all time in Japan.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-32) It then had its fourth consecutive weekend at number one, drawing another $3 million at 354 locations in the country.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-33) Its cumulative total stands at $44 million grossed.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-34)
_Ted_ debuted with $14.3 million in the United Kingdom, making it the third-best debut ever for a Universal film behind _Bridget Jones: The Edge of Reason_ and _King Kong_,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-Foreign1-35) eventually grossing over $48.9 million in the country. _Ted_ was released in cinemas across the United Kingdom on August 3.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-ForeignGross-29)

_Ted_ also debuted at number one in Australia and New Zealand, grossing over $35.5 million and $3.5 million respectively.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-ForeignGross-29) Its $13.1 million opening in Australia, of which $4.5 million were from previews, was Universal's biggest opening ever in the country.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-Australia_Record-27) In Australia, _Ted_ was rated MA 15+,[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-Aus-49) whereas in New Zealand, it was rated R13 for its theatrical release and R16 for the extended DVD/Blu-ray release.
South America  
In Brazil, the film opened with $1.4 million at 273 sites,[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-50) moving up to 1st place in the country on its third week of release.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-51) It has since grossed $8.8 million there.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-ForeignGross-29)
The film also grossed $4.6 million in Argentina, 2 million in Chile, 1.9 million in Peru, and 1.7 million in Colombia.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-ForeignGross-29)

Most of the reviews _Ted_ received were positive.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-54)On the review aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes, 68% of 219 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 6.40/10.The website's consensus reads: "_Ted_'s 'romance versus bromance' plot is familiar, but the film's held aloft by the high-concept central premise and a very funny (albeit inconsistent) script."[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-Rotten_Tomatoes-55) On Metacritic, the film has an average score of 62 out of 100 based on 37 critics, indicating "generally favorable reviews".[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-Metacritic-56) Audiences polled by CinemaScore gave the film an average grade of "A−" on an A+ to F scale.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-CinemaScore-57)
Roger Ebert gave the film three-and-a-half stars out of four, citing the film as "the best comedy screenplay so far [this year]," also praising the film on the fact that it "doesn't run out of steam."[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-RE-58)Nathan Rabin of _The A.V. Club_ gave the film a "B" grade.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-AVClub-59) On the other hand, A.O. Scott of _The New York Times_ called _Ted_ "boring, lazy and wildly unoriginal."[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-NYT-60)

Director Paul Thomas Anderson has stated that he is a big fan of the film, calling it great and also putting it on his favorite films of the 21st century list.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-62)
The film was released on DVD and Blu-ray in the United States on December 11, 2012, by Universal Studios Home Entertainment.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-78) Both formats featured an unrated version of the film (112 minutes) and were also released in Australia on November 21, 2012, in an "Extended Edition".[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-79) It was released on DVD and Blu-ray in the United Kingdom on November 26, 2012.
On May 3, 2016, _Ted vs. Flash Gordon: The Ultimate Collection_ was released on Blu-ray plus Digital HD, featuring _Flash Gordon_ and the unrated versions of _Ted_ and _Ted 2_.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-80)
_Ted_ was released on 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray as a [collector's edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collector's_edition "Collector's edition") on December 10, 2024, by Shout! Factory.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-81)
In Brazil, the movie was the target of a complaint from a member of the PCDB party, who denounced the film for promoting drug use and requested its suspension, calling it absurd.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-82)

During the 2012 _American Dad!_Comic-Con panel, MacFarlane stated that he would be open to a sequel to _Ted_.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-83) In September 2012, chief executive Steve Burke said that the studio would be looking to make a sequel to _Ted_ "as soon as possible".[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-84)
On _Anderson Live_, Wahlberg confirmed that a sequel was in the works and that it would be the first sequel in his career, while also revealing that he and Ted (as voiced by MacFarlane) would appear at the 85th Academy Awards.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-85)
In February 2014, _Deadline_ reported that Amanda Seyfried had been cast as the female lead, and that Kunis would not return.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-86) On July 8, MacFarlane announced that work had officially begun on the sequel.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-87)_Ted 2_ was released in the United States on June 26, 2015.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_(film)#cite_note-88) It was neither critically nor financially as successful, though it still turned a profit, grossing $215.9 million on a $68 million budget.

## Who Did Ted End Up With on ‘How I Met Your Mother’? How the Finale Wrapped Up His Journey
Ron P. Jaffe / ©CBS / courtesy Everett Collection
Ted (Josh Radnor) spent nine seasons looking for the love of his life on _How I Met Your Mother_. He almost tied the knot with Stella (Sarah Chalke), and often had to deal with his lingering feelings for Robin (Cobie Smulders), but during the series finale he finally married the mother of his two children.
However, Ted’s life was always more complicated than simply being able to have a happy ending. Scroll down for a refresh on what happened and who he actually ended up with at the end of the series.
At the very end of the Season 9 finale, it was revealed that Ted ended up with Robin. After Ted’s kids finally heard the conclusion of the story of how he met their mother, Tracy (Cristin Milioti), who died six years earlier, they were the ones who helped him realize that he was in love with “aunt Robin.”
“Come on, dad, mom’s been gone for six years now. It’s time,” Penny (Lyndsy Fonseca) told him, prompting Ted to race over to Robin’s apartment with the iconic blue french horn from their first date. As he showed it to her from outside the window, she flashed a huge smile, signaling that she was also on board for their romantic reconciliation.
Carin Baer / © CBS / Everett Collection
Prior to finally getting together with Robin, Ted lived a happy life with Tracy for about ten years. They met at Robin and Barney’s (Neil Patrick Harris) wedding in 2013 and immediately connected, which helped Ted move on from the fact that Robin was marrying his best friend. Ted and Tracy put off their nuptials when he became pregnant with their first child in 2015, followed by baby No. 2 in 2017. They got married in 2020, but she soon got sick. Ted was by her side through her illness, which she succumbed to in 2024.
It then took six years to finally pursue Robin once again.

## What happened to Barney on _HIMYM_?
Wait, why was Robin available to be pursued by Ted if she was married to Barney? Well, the pair’s marriage only lasted three years. They divorced in 2016. Let’s face it, Barney was never meant to be a married man. Even though he was in love with Robin and pulled off the ultimate playbook move to propose to her, he was always going to put himself first at the end of the day. Plus, Robin was too invested in her career to make her marriage to Barney a success.
Ron P. Jaffe / ©CBS / Everett Collection
After the divorce, Barney went back to his playboy ways, but ultimately found the love of his life in the form of his daughter, Ellie, born in 2020. Ellie was conceived while Barney was trying to perfect a “perfect month” in August 2019 and impregnated the woman from day 31.
While having kids was never on Barney’s radar in the past, there was no denying the love he felt when he held his baby girl for the first time.

## Do Lily and Marshall get divorced on _HIMYM_?
No, of course not! They’re Marshmallow and Lilypad! However, the end of the series didn’t come without some struggles for the couple. Lily (Alyson Hannigan) was excited to have a job offer in Rome, while Marshall (Jason Segel) received an offer to become a judge in New York. However, when Lily revealed that she was pregnant with their second child, Marshall knew it was time to put his dreams on hold.
Richard Cartwright / ©CBS / courtesy Everett Collection
The family moved to Rome with their little family and Lily pursued her art passion, but the flash forward sequence in the finale revealed that Marshall eventually got his dream too. In 2020, he was elected as a Supreme Court judge. The pair also had a third child at some point in the future.

After nine seasons, countless “legendary” moments and one very long story, _How I Met Your Mother_ delivered a finale that left some fans scratching their heads.
The sitcom, which aired from 2005 to 2014, chronicled the lives of Ted Mosby (Josh Radnor) and his close-knit group of friends in New York City. The series is framed around Ted's narration (Bob Saget) to his children, Penny (Lyndsy Fonseca) and Luke (David Henrie), about the events leading up to his meeting their mother.
After nine seasons of intricate storytelling, the series finale delivered a conclusion that left fans divided. While some felt it was a fitting end, others believed it unraveled key character arcs built over the years.
Here’s everything to know about the ending of _How I Met Your Mother_, 12 years after it aired.
**Warning: Spoilers ahead for the series finale of _How I Met Your Mother_.**

## How did _How I Met Your Mother_ end?
Josh Radnor and Cristin Milioti in 'How I Met Your Mother'.  
CBS / courtesy Everett Collection
In the final episode, Ted met Tracy McConnell (Cristin Milioti), the titular mother, at the Farhampton train station, leading to a loving relationship and the birth of their two children. However, it's later revealed that Tracy died after a prolonged illness.
In 2030, Ted's children, having heard their father's story, encourage him to pursue a romantic relationship with Robin Scherbatsky (Cobie Smulders), his longtime friend and former love interest.
The finale also addressed other main characters' arcs: Barney Stinson (Neil Patrick Harris) and Robin end up divorcing, while Marshall Eriksen (Jason Segel) and Lily Aldrin (Alyson Hannigan) expand their family.

## Did Ted end up with Robin?
Cobie Smulders and Josh Radnor in 'How I Met Your Mother'.  
Carin Baer / © CBS / Courtesy Everett Collection
Ted and Robin’s relationship was one of the most debated aspects of _How I Met Your Mother_, and the series finale ultimately confirmed that their story wasn’t over. While Ted spent nine seasons recounting the journey of how he met Tracy, the final moments of the show revealed that Tracy had passed away years prior.
In a surprising twist, Ted’s children encouraged him to go after their “Aunt” Robin, recognizing that the entire story he had told them was more about her than their late mother.
The series concluded with Ted standing outside Robin’s apartment, holding the blue French horn — a callback to their romantic history in the pilot episode when Ted stole it for Robin after she saw it on their first date.
From this point onwards, Robin kept it on the mantle in her apartment.

## Did Barney end up single?
Neil Patrick Harris and Cobie Smulders in 'How I Met Your Mother'.  
Neil Jacobs / ©CBS / courtesy Everett Collection
By the end of the show, Barney’s love life took an unexpected turn. After years of being known as a womanizer, Barney settled down and married Robin in the show's final season.
However, their marriage was short-lived, lasting only three years before they divorced due to their conflicting lifestyles —Robin’s demanding career as a journalist kept her traveling, while Barney struggled to adapt to a committed relationship.
Following the divorce, Barney seemingly returned to his bachelor ways. However, his life took a significant turn when he unexpectedly became a father from a one-night stand. This moment was a turning point for him — despite his past indifference toward settling down, fatherhood changed him completely.
In one of the most emotional scenes of the finale, Barney held his newborn daughter and told her, "You are the love of my life. Everything I have and everything I am is yours forever."

## Where did Marshall and Lily end up?
Alyson Hannigan as Lily and Jason Segel as Marshall in 'How I Met Your Mother'.  
Richard Cartwright/CBS via Getty
Marshall and Lily remained the most stable couple in the group. He achieved his long-standing dream of becoming a judge, earning the nickname "Judge Fudge" along the way.
Eventually, he reached an even higher milestone in his legal career when he was elected to the New York Supreme Court. Meanwhile, Lily continued to thrive in her art career, though much of her focus remained on their growing family.
Throughout the series, the couple navigated major life changes, including Lily’s brief move to San Francisco after breaking off her engagement with Marshall, plus arguments about their respective careers.
Eventually, the pair married and welcomed two children together, Marvin (named after Marshall’s father) and Daisy. In the finale, it’s revealed that they have a third child.

## Why were fans so divided on the finale?
Josh Radnor in 'How I Met Your Mother'.  
CBS
The _HIMYM_ finale sparked heated debate, with many fans feeling it downplayed the story’s emotional payoff. After spending nine seasons building up Ted and Tracy’s love story, the revelation that she dies and Ted ultimately reunites with Robin felt abrupt and unsatisfying to some viewers.
Many argued that the show had spent years proving why Ted and Robin weren’t meant to be, only to reverse course in the final moments.
Others defended the ending as a realistic portrayal of love and loss, with Ted’s journey coming full circle. The creators, Carter Bays and Craig Thomas, had planned the conclusion from the beginning, even filming Ted’s kids’ reaction years in advance.
While some appreciated the callback to the blue French horn, others felt the finale rushed through key character developments and reduced Tracy to a mere plot device.
After the finale aired in 2014, Thomas thanked his fans for their support.
“We did a finale about life’s twists and turns and that is not always what happens … but THANKS!” he wrote on X.

## Will there be any spinoffs or revivals?
Cobie Smulders in 'How I Met Your Father'.Patrick Wymore/Hulu
While _How I Met Your Mother_ officially ended in 2014, the franchise was briefly revived with _How I Met Your Father_, a spinoff starring Hilary Duff that premiered on Hulu in January 2022.
With a similar concept — Sophie (Duff) recounts the story of how she met her son’s father — the show exists in the same universe as _HIMYM_ but has minimal connections to the original series.
Though there were occasional callbacks, such as the reappearance of the MacLaren’s Pub set and a cameo from Smulders as Robin, the show largely focused on a new cast and storyline.
Despite an initial wave of excitement, Hulu canceled the series after two seasons in 2023, leaving its central mystery unresolved.
As of now, there are no official plans for a _How I Met Your Mother_ revival. Radnor and Thomas did team up in 2025, however, for an official rewatch podcast, _How We Made Your Mother__._

# _How I Met Your Mother_ Ending Explained: So, How _Did_ Ted Meet Their Mother?
### What happens to Barney and Robin?
Surprise! Three years after their wedding, these two get divorced. Robin’s career with World Wide News takes off and she’s sent all over the globe. The two of them are miserable in that situation, and, quite amicably, decide to end things. They promise it won’t change anything, but well, you can guess how well that works out.
Barney returns to his womanizing ways until something quite unexpected happens: One of his hookups during his “perfect month” winds up pregnant and he has a daughter named Ellie in 2020. Tearfully, he holds her in his arms and says to her the thing he swore he’d never say to a woman upon first sight: “You are the love of my life. Everything I have and everything I am is yours forever.”
Robin tries to stay close with the gang, but finds it too difficult to be around not just Barney, but a happily-in-love Ted, who, she tells Lily, is the guy she “probably should’ve ended up with.” She breaks Lily’s heart by cutting herself out of the group. It’s not forever, though: Robin bumps into Ted with his daughter Penny (Cristina N. Rose) on the street one day and then eventually shows up for Ted and Tracy’s wedding. The gang’s back together.
Ron Jaffe/CBS via Getty Images

# _How I Met Your Mother_ Ending Explained: So, How _Did_ Ted Meet Their Mother?
### What happens to Ted at the end of _How I Met Your Mother_?
When Ted ends his story with “and that, kids, is how I met your mother,” his kids call bull. That was very much a long and meandering story about how Ted is completely in love with their Aunt Robin — almost as if he wants their permission to finally go for it. It’s been six years since their mom died and Ted is never happier than when Robin is around, of course he needs to go for it, they tell him.
And so Ted does. He runs to Robin’s apartment and in a callback to the pilot episode, Robin opens up her window and finds Ted standing on the street holding that blue French horn from the restaurant where they had their very first date.

After nine seasons, countless “legendary” moments and one very long story, _How I Met Your Mother_ delivered a finale that left some fans scratching their heads.
The sitcom, which aired from 2005 to 2014, chronicled the lives of Ted Mosby (Josh Radnor) and his close-knit group of friends in New York City. The series is framed around Ted's narration (Bob Saget) to his children, Penny (Lyndsy Fonseca) and Luke (David Henrie), about the events leading up to his meeting their mother.
After nine seasons of intricate storytelling, the series finale delivered a conclusion that left fans divided. While some felt it was a fitting end, others believed it unraveled key character arcs built over the years.
Here’s everything to know about the ending of _How I Met Your Mother_, 12 years after it aired.
**Warning: Spoilers ahead for the series finale of _How I Met Your Mother_.**

## How did _How I Met Your Mother_ end?
Josh Radnor and Cristin Milioti in 'How I Met Your Mother'.  
CBS / courtesy Everett Collection
In the final episode, Ted met Tracy McConnell (Cristin Milioti), the titular mother, at the Farhampton train station, leading to a loving relationship and the birth of their two children. However, it's later revealed that Tracy died after a prolonged illness.
In 2030, Ted's children, having heard their father's story, encourage him to pursue a romantic relationship with Robin Scherbatsky (Cobie Smulders), his longtime friend and former love interest.
The finale also addressed other main characters' arcs: Barney Stinson (Neil Patrick Harris) and Robin end up divorcing, while Marshall Eriksen (Jason Segel) and Lily Aldrin (Alyson Hannigan) expand their family.
texts.2:
## Did Ted end up with Robin?
Cobie Smulders and Josh Radnor in 'How I Met Your Mother'.  
Carin Baer / © CBS / Courtesy Everett Collection
Ted and Robin’s relationship was one of the most debated aspects of _How I Met Your Mother_, and the series finale ultimately confirmed that their story wasn’t over. While Ted spent nine seasons recounting the journey of how he met Tracy, the final moments of the show revealed that Tracy had passed away years prior.
In a surprising twist, Ted’s children encouraged him to go after their “Aunt” Robin, recognizing that the entire story he had told them was more about her than their late mother.
The series concluded with Ted standing outside Robin’s apartment, holding the blue French horn — a callback to their romantic history in the pilot episode when Ted stole it for Robin after she saw it on their first date.
From this point onwards, Robin kept it on the mantle in her apartment.
texts.3:
## Did Barney end up single?
Neil Patrick Harris and Cobie Smulders in 'How I Met Your Mother'.  
Neil Jacobs / ©CBS / courtesy Everett Collection
By the end of the show, Barney’s love life took an unexpected turn. After years of being known as a womanizer, Barney settled down and married Robin in the show's final season.
However, their marriage was short-lived, lasting only three years before they divorced due to their conflicting lifestyles —Robin’s demanding career as a journalist kept her traveling, while Barney struggled to adapt to a committed relationship.
Following the divorce, Barney seemingly returned to his bachelor ways. However, his life took a significant turn when he unexpectedly became a father from a one-night stand. This moment was a turning point for him — despite his past indifference toward settling down, fatherhood changed him completely.
In one of the most emotional scenes of the finale, Barney held his newborn daughter and told her, "You are the love of my life. Everything I have and everything I am is yours forever."
texts.4:
## Where did Marshall and Lily end up?
Alyson Hannigan as Lily and Jason Segel as Marshall in 'How I Met Your Mother'.  
Richard Cartwright/CBS via Getty
Marshall and Lily remained the most stable couple in the group. He achieved his long-standing dream of becoming a judge, earning the nickname "Judge Fudge" along the way.
Eventually, he reached an even higher milestone in his legal career when he was elected to the New York Supreme Court. Meanwhile, Lily continued to thrive in her art career, though much of her focus remained on their growing family.
Throughout the series, the couple navigated major life changes, including Lily’s brief move to San Francisco after breaking off her engagement with Marshall, plus arguments about their respective careers.
Eventually, the pair married and welcomed two children together, Marvin (named after Marshall’s father) and Daisy. In the finale, it’s revealed that they have a third child.
texts.5:
## Why were fans so divided on the finale?
Josh Radnor in 'How I Met Your Mother'.  
CBS
The _HIMYM_ finale sparked heated debate, with many fans feeling it downplayed the story’s emotional payoff. After spending nine seasons building up Ted and Tracy’s love story, the revelation that she dies and Ted ultimately reunites with Robin felt abrupt and unsatisfying to some viewers.
Many argued that the show had spent years proving why Ted and Robin weren’t meant to be, only to reverse course in the final moments.
Others defended the ending as a realistic portrayal of love and loss, with Ted’s journey coming full circle. The creators, Carter Bays and Craig Thomas, had planned the conclusion from the beginning, even filming Ted’s kids’ reaction years in advance.
While some appreciated the callback to the blue French horn, others felt the finale rushed through key character developments and reduced Tracy to a mere plot device.
After the finale aired in 2014, Thomas thanked his fans for their support.
“We did a finale about life’s twists and turns and that is not always what happens … but THANKS!” he wrote on X.

## Will there be any spinoffs or revivals?
Cobie Smulders in 'How I Met Your Father'.Patrick Wymore/Hulu
While _How I Met Your Mother_ officially ended in 2014, the franchise was briefly revived with _How I Met Your Father_, a spinoff starring Hilary Duff that premiered on Hulu in January 2022.
With a similar concept — Sophie (Duff) recounts the story of how she met her son’s father — the show exists in the same universe as _HIMYM_ but has minimal connections to the original series.
Though there were occasional callbacks, such as the reappearance of the MacLaren’s Pub set and a cameo from Smulders as Robin, the show largely focused on a new cast and storyline.
Despite an initial wave of excitement, Hulu canceled the series after two seasons in 2023, leaving its central mystery unresolved.
As of now, there are no official plans for a _How I Met Your Mother_ revival. Radnor and Thomas did team up in 2025, however, for an official rewatch podcast, _How We Made Your Mother__._

## Who Did Ted End Up With on ‘How I Met Your Mother’? How the Finale Wrapped Up His Journey
Ron P. Jaffe / ©CBS / courtesy Everett Collection
Ted (Josh Radnor) spent nine seasons looking for the love of his life on _How I Met Your Mother_. He almost tied the knot with Stella (Sarah Chalke), and often had to deal with his lingering feelings for Robin (Cobie Smulders), but during the series finale he finally married the mother of his two children.
However, Ted’s life was always more complicated than simply being able to have a happy ending. Scroll down for a refresh on what happened and who he actually ended up with at the end of the series.
At the very end of the Season 9 finale, it was revealed that Ted ended up with Robin. After Ted’s kids finally heard the conclusion of the story of how he met their mother, Tracy (Cristin Milioti), who died six years earlier, they were the ones who helped him realize that he was in love with “aunt Robin.”
“Come on, dad, mom’s been gone for six years now. It’s time,” Penny (Lyndsy Fonseca) told him, prompting Ted to race over to Robin’s apartment with the iconic blue french horn from their first date. As he showed it to her from outside the window, she flashed a huge smile, signaling that she was also on board for their romantic reconciliation.
Carin Baer / © CBS / Everett Collection
Prior to finally getting together with Robin, Ted lived a happy life with Tracy for about ten years. They met at Robin and Barney’s (Neil Patrick Harris) wedding in 2013 and immediately connected, which helped Ted move on from the fact that Robin was marrying his best friend. Ted and Tracy put off their nuptials when he became pregnant with their first child in 2015, followed by baby No. 2 in 2017. They got married in 2020, but she soon got sick. Ted was by her side through her illness, which she succumbed to in 2024.
It then took six years to finally pursue Robin once again.

## What happened to Barney on _HIMYM_?
Wait, why was Robin available to be pursued by Ted if she was married to Barney? Well, the pair’s marriage only lasted three years. They divorced in 2016. Let’s face it, Barney was never meant to be a married man. Even though he was in love with Robin and pulled off the ultimate playbook move to propose to her, he was always going to put himself first at the end of the day. Plus, Robin was too invested in her career to make her marriage to Barney a success.
Ron P. Jaffe / ©CBS / Everett Collection
After the divorce, Barney went back to his playboy ways, but ultimately found the love of his life in the form of his daughter, Ellie, born in 2020. Ellie was conceived while Barney was trying to perfect a “perfect month” in August 2019 and impregnated the woman from day 31.
While having kids was never on Barney’s radar in the past, there was no denying the love he felt when he held his baby girl for the first time.
texts.3:
## Do Lily and Marshall get divorced on _HIMYM_?
No, of course not! They’re Marshmallow and Lilypad! However, the end of the series didn’t come without some struggles for the couple. Lily (Alyson Hannigan) was excited to have a job offer in Rome, while Marshall (Jason Segel) received an offer to become a judge in New York. However, when Lily revealed that she was pregnant with their second child, Marshall knew it was time to put his dreams on hold.
Richard Cartwright / ©CBS / courtesy Everett Collection
The family moved to Rome with their little family and Lily pursued her art passion, but the flash forward sequence in the finale revealed that Marshall eventually got his dream too. In 2020, he was elected as a Supreme Court judge. The pair also had a third child at some point in the future.

The _HIMYM_ finale sparked heated debate, with many fans feeling it downplayed the story’s emotional payoff. After spending nine seasons building up Ted and Tracy’s love story, the revelation that she dies and Ted ultimately reunites with Robin felt abrupt and unsatisfying to some viewers.
Many argued that the show had spent years proving why Ted and Robin weren’t meant to be, only to reverse course in the final moments.
Others defended the ending as a realistic portrayal of love and loss, with Ted’s journey coming full circle. The creators, Carter Bays and Craig Thomas, had planned the conclusion from the beginning, even filming Ted’s kids’ reaction years in advance.
While some appreciated the callback to the blue French horn, others felt the finale rushed through key character developments and reduced Tracy to a mere plot device.
After the finale aired in 2014, Thomas thanked his fans for their support.

Cobie Smulders in 'How I Met Your Father'.Patrick Wymore/Hulu
While _How I Met Your Mother_ officially ended in 2014, the franchise was briefly revived with _How I Met Your Father_, a spinoff starring Hilary Duff that premiered on Hulu in January 2022.
With a similar concept — Sophie (Duff) recounts the story of how she met her son’s father — the show exists in the same universe as _HIMYM_ but has minimal connections to the original series.
Though there were occasional callbacks, such as the reappearance of the MacLaren’s Pub set and a cameo from Smulders as Robin, the show largely focused on a new cast and storyline.
Despite an initial wave of excitement, Hulu canceled the series after two seasons in 2023, leaving its central mystery unresolved.
As of now, there are no official plans for a _How I Met Your Mother_ revival. Radnor and Thomas did team up in 2025, however, for an official rewatch podcast, _How We Made Your Mother__._
